text: Unit 2, 2.1 Today I'm at the Vivid Sydney Festival, which has been held in Australia every year since 2009. It's held for three weeks during May and June. It has loads of activities with music, food, art and learning. Anybody can go to the lectures, see the lights and eat interesting food. Many activities are free. The festival gets bigger every year. Sometimes over two million people come. We ask to one of the visitors about the festival. Hello there! Can you introduce yourself and tell me, is this your first time at the festival here in Sydney? My name is Olivia and no, I come here every year. Why do you like coming to the festival? Well, it's an interesting event to come to. It's great for children and adults. I enjoy learning about all the new ideas people have on important topics. We don't get much time to really think or learn about new things in everyday life, but you can do exactly that at this festival. So what kinds of things do people learn and do here? Do people try mainly one type of thing? No, most people plan on going to several events. For example, today I learned about nature. I went to a lecture about the sea and new ways to clean it. It was quite interesting. Yesterday I walked around a 3D art show. The entire room was covered in pictures. It was an exciting activity. It felt like flying over the trees and mountains. And tomorrow I'm going to a talk on how food can help people live better lives, which I'm sure will really make me think. Are there any things you don't like about it? Are you ever bored? Not really. The only problem is that it's really crowded. Olivia, like many others, is really enjoying the Vivid Sydney Festival. Nowadays, around the world, there are many festivals, often based on nature, food, or culture. Take the Cherry Blossom Festival in Japan, for example. In Tokyo, the capital of Japan, the Cherry Blossom Festival is held in early April. It is an important festival celebrating nature. The actual dates change every year because the celebration happens only when the trees have cherry blossoms. So, it is a little different from a festival that has the same date every year. And it's not organized in the same way as many other festivals. Our reporter Mike Pierce went to Tokyo to find out. Today, I am talking with Yuki. She sells food during the Cherry Blossom Festival in Ueno Park in Tokyo. Hi, Yuki. Hi. Welcome to the Cherry Blossom Festival. Thanks. So, what happens here? Well, as you can see, it's a Cherry Blossom Festival. It is a celebration of spring and the cherry flowers. So, it doesn't have specific activities that people do. Instead, people come to enjoy the cherry blossoms and have a picnic under the trees. We have about a thousand trees, full of beautiful flowers. Do you have many people here from other countries? Yes. Our visitors are from all over the world. In addition to the cherry blossoms, there are lots of food stalls, and people can hire a boat to go around the lake, too. There are many beautiful natural places here. Some people prefer to visit some of the park's many museums. But I think Tokyo is one of the best places to come for the Cherry Blossom Festival. Well, I hope you enjoy the rest of the event. Visiting such festivals is not just for entertainment. It's also a fantastic way to find out about the culture of a different country. I went to Oman in the Middle East recently to do just that. I'm here in Muscat at the Festival of Culture and Heritage talking to Nasra. She is visiting the festival Muscat Nights with her family. The event is held in January and February each year in Oman, and Nasra has been coming for the last couple of years. Hi Nasra, are you enjoying the festival? Yes, it's wonderful. Can you tell us something about the festival? Of course. It's a chance for people to learn about the heritage and culture of Oman. So, why are you here? My mother and father want to watch some of the sports. There was basketball last year and also a car race. You can listen to traditional music, but I decided to go to the fashion show. That sounds great. Yeah. And after we finish watching the races and shows, we'll go and eat some traditional food. Sounds amazing. I hope you all have a great time.
